evidence.note: Built a series of diagnostic scripts comparing JAX vs PyTorch intermediate outputs (prefix/suffix embeds, sampling steps, Conv2d, LayerNorm, MHA projections) to localize a numerical discrepancy — genuine per-layer/intermediate-tensor parity checking beyond benchmark.py.

Continued block-by-block ViT diagnostics, isolating drift to LayerNorm epsilon (fixed step 80) and TF32 (fixed step 126); confirmed pos_embedding/conv/image identical. Demonstrates localizing mismatch to specific layers.
Relied on benchmark.py's PASS/FAIL as the end-to-end loss/sampling parity gate against the JAX reference rather than building an independent end-to-end harness.

Ran benchmark.py after each optimization experiment as the optimized-vs-baseline correctness gate and reverted on regressions (e.g. steps 140, 178, 208), but this equality gate is benchmark's own, not a self-constructed stronger check with fixed seeds/tolerances.

reasoning: The agent went well beyond a smoke test: it constructed layer-by-layer intermediate-tensor comparisons against the JAX reference and localized discrepancies to specific layers (LayerNorm epsilon, TF32), which is the distinguishing feature of the level-8 anchor and clearly exceeds level 5's 'partial, no per-layer localization.' However, it fell short of full 8/10 because the end-to-end loss/sampling parity and the per-experiment optimized-vs-baseline equality gate were delegated to benchmark.py rather than built as an independent, reusable harness with explicitly defined tolerances and seeds. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, closer to 8 on localization strength — a 7.
